protocol: trusted local catalog JSON-RPC v1; additive; no AHP or ACP core delta

projectSessionVisibility.atomicity: SQLite immediate write transaction: exact-command signature lookup before CAS; all validation and row writes and checkpoint and receipt commit atomically; conflicting source, duplicate URI, missing identity, bad revision or changed command refuses whole batch

result.source: requested owner selector; a persisted owner checkpoint is evidenced only by projectionPresent
result.revision: source checkpoint or0 when absent; unchanged compatibility field
result.indexIncarnation: immutable canonical UUID persisted once in existing progress metadata for this derived database
result.projectionPresent: computed boolean: a source-keyed projection row actually exists; not persisted readiness

sessionVisibilityProjectionStatus.atomicity: Identity, actual row presence and checkpoint are read in one SQLite statement/snapshot from the active handle. Invalid or missing identity refuses; status never repairs it.

storage: Separate product-only derived visibility/checkpoint/command tables. No native_visibility writes. Host owns canonical reset, retained before-images and no-replay journals; catalog receipts are only rebuildable projection evidence.
readEffects: Filter hidden rows before root/child/archive/retention pagination; exact get exposes productHidden. Descendant and directory-use guards include hidden histories. Metadata/native restore/workspace recheck do not revive hidden product rows.
resetAndUndo: Host first verifies eligibility, exact retained selection and held maintenance. Reset projects hidden:true. Fresh revision-bound retained restore projects exact prior hidden flags at newer revisions. Catalog does not grant reset/deletion authority or inspect foreign receipts.
rebuild: Host rebuilds derived catalog from its retained visibility records in bounded batches. Catalog checkpoint resets to 0 on DB loss. For indexed-only proposal, host must fence listing until facts and visibility projection reconstruction are complete.
preserved: host accepted and unknown input provenance
acceptance: changed-command rejection and exact retry after restart
atomic rollback on mixed valid/invalid batch
native restore and metadata discovery cannot revive hidden rows
restore does not bypass native deletion or workspace exclusion
metadata-only source and installed package checks
4000-workspace 25000/100000-session fixture and hidden-row query work bound
rebuildHandshake: Host-owned durable unavailable fence; immutable stable-URI paged snapshot; reconstruct identities; checkpoint0 replay in max100 contiguous projection sequence batches with exact epoch/page commands; reconcile original receipts; drain subsequent changes; release only after final checkpoint and row-count manifest verify. README is normative for host handshake.

indexContinuity.storage: Transactional insert-if-absent dedicated index-incarnation key in existing progress; no new table, checkpoint, ledger or ready bit
indexContinuity.retention: Reopen, discovery and in-place schema migration preserve identity; a new or recreated database gets a different UUID. Legacy metadata migration adds identity without changing rows/checkpoints/receipts or granting Host readiness.
indexContinuity.consumers: Host acknowledgment belongs only in existing Host authority at its verified qualification boundary. Old Catalog missing additive fields uses the old qualified path with no invented acknowledgment; old Host keeps its existing gating. This Catalog slice does not implement retained-browse admission.
indexContinuity.limits: File copy/backup restore retains the UUID and cannot certify rollback freshness. Restore requires owner fencing and requalification. Live database file replacement while Catalog is serving is unsupported: stop owners and reopen/requalify; surrounding status reads do not prove page origin under arbitrary A-B-A replacement.
